notes: The ground this area owns (3.84 ha): the two ponds west of Lot 45 and south-west of Lot 60, which the roadmap calls the Peckman River ponds, the wooded spit between them and the floor round them, up to the foot of the faces that close them in on the north, west and south-west. Names: OpenStreetMap names neither pond (natural=water, ways 233913170 north and 233913228 south) nor any stream here; 'Peckman River ponds' is the survey's name, UNVERIFIED, and 'ponds' is the folder's label only. The ponds lie outside the university's boundary in OSM (way 233913199, which runs along the Village's west edge here): not campus ground; the Lot 60 area calls the north one 'the pond west of Lot 61 (not university ground)'. No building stands inside. What the LiDAR shows (NJ NW 6-County 2017, 2.9 points per m2): one water level in both ponds (class 9 returns, median 98.61 m, n 7,451), a flat floor of 98.6 to 101 m round them, and on the north, west and south-west near-vertical faces 8 to 25 m high (the ground steps from about 100 to 108..115 m within 1 to 4 m on the north, to 110..125 m on the west and south-west): the apartment parking above the north face and the yards of the houses above the west face stand on top. Whether the faces are rock or built walls is not told by any source here (UNVERIFIED; the ortho shows trees on them). Edges. East: shared with the Village (its west edge, vertex for vertex: (-212, 1281), (-240, 1262), (-292, 1270), (-350, 1253), (-383, 1230), (-390, 1205), (-372, 1160): the lawn and Lot 45 above the east shore stay the Village's) and with Lot 60 (its south-west edge, vertex for vertex: (-196, 1315), (-322, 1366), (-346, 1366), (-364, 1398), (-362, 1413): the bank under the Lot 60 bus lot stays Lot 60's). North, west and south-west: 1 m outside the foot of the faces, so the floor is all inside and the faces stand outside: the foot traced on the LiDAR ground (0.5 m cells of the floor, ground under 101.5 m or water returns, joined to the ponds), moved 1 m out and simplified to 40 straight runs of 3.6 to 46 m (Douglas-Peucker, 1.6 m); the foot wanders 1 to 3 m along the north face, so the runs lie 0 to 3 m outside it. North-east: round the toe of the rock spur at (-375, 1372) and up the narrow floor west of Lot 60 to Lot 60's corner (-362, 1413). North-west: straight across the low wooded ground at x -515 from y 1294 to 1340 (99.6 to 101.7 m; the floor runs on west to x -565 under the apartments' slope, left out). South: one straight run from the Village's corner (-372, 1160) to the face's foot at (-393.5, 1143), across the bottom of the slope that climbs south-east out of the pit (OSM draws water there; the LiDAR has dry ground rising from 100 to 123 m). Neighbours outside the shared edges: the 4 km context skirt only (triangles about 10 m across): it smooths each face into a slope over about 20 m, so at the foot it stands 3 to 6 m over the LiDAR floor and on top 3 to 7 m under it; the soft ground bends to it over 4 m inside the edge (BLEND), so the edge reads as a steep bank and the faces as the skirt's slope (UNVERIFIED shape of the faces). No path, bridge, wall, paving or fence shows inside in the 2020 ortho, the LiDAR or OSM: the spit between the ponds is a wooded ridge 3 to 4 m wide whose crest stands 0.3 to 0.45 m over the water (no trail can be seen under the trees); OSM's footways near (-513..-460, 1407..1507) belong to the apartments outside. Joe's photos (refs/joe_20261120) show Alumni Green, Cole Hall, Kasser Theater and the College of Communication and Media: none shows this place. Evidence: /workspace/data/ponds (NJ 2020 ortho 0.15 m, x -600..-150, y 960..1440; LiDAR 2017 0.5 m, x -600..-140, y 960..1460; OSM 2026-11-22; a dump of the published sw17 tiles).

supersede.notes: Patterns match 'mesh name material name' in the other sources' tiles. clip: their ground inside the footprint (triangle area with its centre inside, m2, from a dump of the published sw17 tiles: Context_skirt_3DEP_ortho_4km 38,440 (622 triangles); BD_farfield_3DEP, North_ground_ortho2020 and MH_ground_ortho2020 0, kept as in the neighbours so that any of their ground under the outline goes too). drop: far_houses (none inside: every far-field house stands on top of the faces, outside; kept so that a house mapped later inside is not left standing in the pond). Far-field trees inside are removed by the export. overlap: along the edges shared with the Village and Lot 60 the cut reaches 0.6 m into them (supersede.OVERLAP), so no sliver of the skirt stands between the two areas' cuts.
